title: Exploring the interplay between Porphyromonas gingivalis KGP gingipain, herpes virus MicroRNA-6, and Icp4 transcript in periodontitis: Computational and clinical insights.
authors: Yadalam, Pradeep Kumar; Neelakandan, Anila; Arunraj, Rex; Anegundi, Raghavendra Vamsi; Ardila, Carlos M
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子对接研究牙龈卟啉单胞菌KGP蛋白酶与HSV ICP4转录因子的结合，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作和对接方法，但对象非典型TF-DNA体系且临床部分为主，深度不足。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Porphyromonas gingivalis, a major pathogen in periodontitis, produces KGP (Lys-gingipain), a cysteine protease that enhances bacterial virulence by promoting tissue invasion and immune evasion. Recent studies highlight microRNAs' role in viral latency, potentially affecting lytic replication through host mechanisms. Herpes virus (HSV) establishes latency via interactions between microRNA-6 (miRH-6) and the ICP4 transcription factor in neural ganglia. This suggests a potential link between periodontitis and HSV-induced latency. This study aims to identify and validate the insilico inhibitory interaction of P. gingivalis KGP with ICP4 transcripts and correlate the presence of viral latency-associated transcript micro-RNA-6 with periodontitis. METHODS: Computational docking analysis was performed to investigate the potential interaction between ICP4 and KGP gingipain. The binding energy and RMSD ligand values were calculated to determine the interaction's strength. Ten patients with recurrent clinical attachment loss despite conventional therapy were included in the clinical study. Subgingival tissue samples were collected post-phase I therapy, and HSV microRNA-6 presence was detected via polymerase chain reaction and confirmed through gel electrophoresis. RESULTS: Computational docking identified the ICP4-KGP gingipain complex with the lowest binding energy (-288.29 kJ mol;1) and an RMSD ligand of 1.5 Angstroms, indicating strong interaction potential. Gel electrophoresis confirmed miRH-6 presence in all samples. CONCLUSION: The identification of miRNA-6 in periodontitis patients and the strong interaction potential between P. gingivalis KGP gingipain and ICP4 transcripts indicate a possible link between bacterial virulence factors and viral latency dynamics in periodontal tissues. These results highlight the complex interplay between oral pathogens, viral microRNAs, and host immune responses in periodontitis.
abstract_zh: 背景：牙龈卟啉单胞菌（Porphyromonas gingivalis）是牙周炎的主要病原体，产生KGP（赖氨酸牙龈蛋白酶），一种通过促进组织侵袭和免疫逃逸增强细菌毒力的半胱氨酸蛋白酶。近期研究强调microRNA在病毒潜伏期中的作用，可能通过宿主机制影响裂解性复制。疱疹病毒（HSV）通过microRNA-6（miRH-6）与神经节中ICP4转录因子之间的相互作用建立潜伏期。这表明牙周炎与HSV诱导的潜伏期之间存在潜在联系。本研究旨在识别并验证牙龈卟啉单胞菌KGP与ICP4转录本的计算机模拟抑制性相互作用，并将病毒潜伏相关转录本microRNA-6的存在与牙周炎相关联。方法：进行计算对接分析，以研究ICP4与KGP牙龈蛋白酶之间的潜在相互作用。计算结合能和RMSD配体值以确定相互作用的强度。临床研究纳入10名尽管接受常规治疗仍出现复发性临床附着丧失的患者。在I期治疗后收集龈下组织样本，通过聚合酶链反应检测HSV microRNA-6的存在，并通过凝胶电泳确认。结果：计算对接识别出ICP4-KGP牙龈蛋白酶复合物具有最低结合能（-288.29 kJ mol;1）和1.5埃的RMSD配体值，表明强相互作用潜力。凝胶电泳确认所有样本中均存在miRH-6。结论：在牙周炎患者中识别出miRNA-6，以及牙龈卟啉单胞菌KGP牙龈蛋白酶与ICP4转录本之间的强相互作用潜力，表明细菌毒力因子与牙周组织中病毒潜伏动态之间存在可能联系。这些结果突显了口腔病原体、病毒microRNA和宿主免疫反应在牙周炎中的复杂相互作用。
